class.name: NetwSceneConfig
class.brief_description: The declaration that makes a node a multiplayer scene.
class.description:
Answered by [method Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene] and configured in place. A scene declares itself once from its own root, and that declaration is the only one: there is no second marking step and nothing else has to know the scene exists. The facts land on the root's [b]script[/b], not on this object, so nothing holds the config afterwards and a second instance of the same scene is declared the same way without re-running anything. The verbs may be called in any order. [codeblock] extends Node2D
func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene(self).labeled(&"Level1").isolated() [/codeblock] Declare from [method Object._init], because the declaration is consumed once at [method NetwEntity.arm] and has to ride the SPAWN packet. Declaring writes [member NetwEntity.declares_scene], so the root owns an admission boundary every descendant entity inherits; nothing else about the entity changes.

method.name: isolated
method.description: Gives the scene its own physics and render world, so geometry overlapping another scene's cannot interact with it. Without this the scene shares the world it is parented into. Only a [Viewport] owns a world in Godot, so an isolated scene needs one and the framework builds it: [method Netw.spawn] answers a [SubViewport] with the authored root inside, and the caller parents that. [b]So the node [method Netw.spawn] returns is not the node the callable built.[/b] The scene is still the authored root. [method Netw.scene], the roster, the admissions and the signals are unchanged, and the viewport carries no identity of its own. The one thing that differs is that the root's [method Node.get_parent] is the viewport rather than the node it was added to. [codeblock] var mount := Netw.spawn(spawn_level1) # a SubViewport worlds.add_child(mount) [/codeblock] [codeblock lang=text] Worlds ┖╴ Level1World (SubViewport) # what spawn answered ┖╴ Level1 (Node2D) # the scene, what the callable built [/codeblock] A [SubViewport] renders to a texture, so whether an isolated scene reaches the screen is the game's decision. See [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_local_changed] for the scene this peer is currently in.

method.name: labeled
method.description: Names the scene for [method Netw.scene]. Defaults to the root node's own name. A label names a kind of scene and never one instance, so two live scenes carrying it make [method Netw.scene] refuse the lookup rather than pick a winner. A game that spawned two arenas holds the handle [method Netw.spawn] gave it instead.

members.member: [constant Netw.SCENE_ISOLATION_OWN_WORLD] once [method isolated] is declared, and [constant Netw.SCENE_ISOLATION_NONE] otherwise.
The stem [method labeled] declared, or the root node's name.
